vibe: The big three AI labs all rolled out cyber-focused models the same week, OpenAI's Astra became the first to cross its own 'Critical' cybersecurity threshold, and SonicWall's SMA1000 zero-days are getting hit again — a genuinely heavy AI-meets-security day.

cyber.title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
cyber.summary: SonicWall's SMA1000 Secure Mobile Access boxes are under active attack again via two zero-days that may chain together for full compromise. Corroborated by The Hacker News and The Register — patch or take exposed SMA1000 devices offline now if you manage any.

cyber.title: Malicious .git Configs Can Make Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Other AI Agents Run Attacker Code
cyber.summary: Researchers found poisoned .git config files can trick AI coding agents — including Claude, Codex, and Cursor — into executing attacker-controlled commands when the agent inspects a repo. Worth a read given how much day-to-day work now runs through these tools.

cyber.title: Six curl CVEs after OpenAI and Anthropic came back with zero
cyber.summary: A security firm ran a traditional audit on curl after AI security-review agents from both OpenAI and Anthropic scanned the same codebase and found nothing — the human-led audit turned up six real CVEs. A useful reality check on how far 'AI finds your vulnerabilities' tooling has actually come. Strong HN discussion (142 pts/50 comments).

cyber.title: Hackers exploit critical JFrog Artifactory flaw to forge admin tokens
cyber.summary: CVE-2026-82329 is being actively exploited to forge admin tokens on JFrog Artifactory instances. Corroborated by Dark Reading, The Register, and securityonline.info — patch and rotate tokens if you run Artifactory.

cyber.title: Critical Langflow Vulnerability Exploited as Attacks on AI Platform Rise
cyber.summary: A critical Langflow vulnerability is being actively exploited as part of a broader wave of credential-probing attacks against AI development platforms — The Hacker News separately reports the same campaign also hitting a Rails flaw.

cyber.title: Sality, one of the longest-running botnets, finally gets disrupted
cyber.summary: A joint law-enforcement and CrowdStrike operation poisoned and sinkholed the Sality botnet's peer-to-peer infrastructure, ending a 23-year run. Corroborated by CyberScoop, The Register, BleepingComputer, and The Hacker News.

cyber.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
cyber.summary: The FBI is investigating a service allegedly offering access to over 153 million US driver's license records. Big HN engagement (359 pts/242 comments) — worth knowing given the scale.

ai.title: Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI Unveil Cyber AI Models, Safeguards, and Access Programs
ai.summary: All three major labs rolled out cyber-focused AI models and safeguard programs the same week. CNBC adds the sharpest detail: OpenAI says its unreleased Astra model is the first to cross its 'Critical' cybersecurity capability threshold — it can find and exploit unknown flaws without step-by-step human guidance, so access to its cyber capabilities will be tightly gated even after release.

ai.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it's up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work
ai.summary: New Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models — up to 45% cheaper for agentic work, 75% cheaper cache reads, and a 52.6% score on Terminal-Bench-Science per MarkTechPost. This is the model line behind your day-to-day Claude use, Tom.

ai.title: Anthropic promises zero data retention — but customers must check it worked
ai.summary: Anthropic revised its data retention policy after enterprise pushback and shipped 'Enterprise Frontier Safeguards' (zero-data-retention plus cross-session misuse detection), confirmed by CNBC — though The Register notes customers still need to verify it's actually working as promised.

ai.title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
ai.summary: The Trump administration formally backed OpenAI's fair-use position in the NYT copyright lawsuit. Corroborated by The Verge and Wired — a meaningful policy signal for the whole industry, not just OpenAI.

ai.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks
ai.summary: Google's third Gemini Flash refresh in six weeks — 'works harder' per Google, though The Verge reports it may also cost more. Big HN thread (659 pts/389 comments).

it.title: Show HN: Aura – a Rust agent that investigates and fixes production incidents
it.summary: Open-source Rust-based on-call agent that investigates and can auto-remediate production incidents. Early-stage (17 pts on HN) but worth a bookmark for SRE/on-call workflows.

videos.title: DOP 366: How to Prevent npm Supply Chain Attacks
videos.verdict: WATCH — dense, concrete interview with Arcjet's David Mitton on npm supply-chain defense: disable pre/post-install scripts, pin dependency versions, use `npm ci` not `npm install`, adopt OIDC trusted publishing plus two-approver staged releases, and set a 7-day cooldown before installing brand-new package versions (catches nearly all recent compromises, including the Axios one that made OpenAI revoke its own signing keys). Genuinely actionable if you touch any JS/TS pipeline.
videos.summary: DevOps Paradox interview covering real, specific npm supply-chain mitigations — dependency pinning, install-script isolation via dev containers/VMs, Renovate cooldown windows, and why 'npm install' alone is a real attack vector in 2026.

videos.title: Why OpenAI is calling for a 'cyber defense surge.' Plus: Find Evil! winners and TeamPCP losers
videos.verdict: SKIM — IBM X-Force panel on OpenAI's open letter (100 orgs signed, incl. IBM) calling for shared threat intel *and* shared remediation, not just IOCs. Also covers SANS's Find Evil hackathon (5 winning open-source AI incident-response harnesses, notable for self-questioning behavior) and how the LiteLLM-breach hackers ('Team PCP') got unmasked in Australia via reused gamer-tag passwords. Skip to the discussion of investigation-vs-response autonomy if short on time — the panel argues AI should investigate incidents but a human should still pull the trigger on remediation actions.
videos.summary: Panel discussion tying together the week's cyber-AI news: the OpenAI-led defense surge letter, an open-source AI incident-response hackathon, and a supply-chain attacker group getting caught by bad password hygiene.
